newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GRABOPLAST ACQUISITIONS KEY TO SUCCESS-CEO.
newsitem.headline: GRABOPLAST ACQUISITIONS KEY TO SUCCESS-CEO.

text.p: Hungarian home improvement product maker group Graboplast, which released last year's consolidated figures on Thursday, said 1996 was a year of successful expansion.
"The holding learned one thing, namely how to integrate (new companies) rapidly," Graboplast Chairman and General Director Peter Jancso told reporters.
In 1996 Graboplast acquired wallpaper factory Kesztolci Tapeta, while in 1995 it had bought Sotex carpet factory and Uniontext textile company.

The results, which were released after close of trade on the Budapest Stock Exchange, showed that the consolidated after-tax profits surged to 1.42 billion forints from 501.1 million in 1995, exceeding plans by 41 percent.
The three acquisitions contributed substantially to the inproivement, Jancso said.
In 1996 Sotex swung to a pre-tax profit of 65.5 million forints from a 1995 loss of 110 million, while Uniontext more than doubled its operating profit to 381 million forints.
Kesztolci wallpaper factory posted a pre-tax profit of 103.5 million forints in 1996 after breakeven in 1995.

The group's sales grew to 15.21 billion in 1996 from 11.59 billion the previous year, but were slightly short of plans, Jancso said. However, Jancso added, both the direct and indirect costs of sales grew at a slower pace than sales.
Graboplast's earnings/share ratio surged to 385 forints from 180 forints, the group said in its earnings report.
Speaking about the group's dividend policy, Jancso said they preferred investors to look at the share price.
"We want to continue to pursue a dividend policy what we've had so far," Jancso said. "We want our share prices rather than our dividend policy to attract investors."

Graboplast said its share prices last year grew 3,670 forints to end the year at 5,470 forints, rising more sharply than the BUX index. Jancso said Graboplast gave a buying order only once last year in November but withdrew it soon afterwards.
The company said it wished in 1997 to continue its expansion and planned to spend 1.7 billion forints on investment.

"The Graboplast-group wishes to develop its already determined strategy which calls for expansion in eastern European markets in the fields of home interior products," Graboplast's earnings report said.

"Accordingly, using the money stemming from a capital increase in 1996, the group wishes to implement new acquisitions with priority on floor cover, parquettry and laminated floor cover, in Hungary and abroad."
In 1997 the group plans to boost its sales to 22.45 billion, its operating profit to 2.18 billion and its pre-tax profit to 2.09 billion.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Graboplast shares closed at 7,720 forints, up 70, as the market closed before the release of the figures.
